To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for breeds S and LW the SEL-BO model is not superior to the BOA or G models, and (ii) for breed LR the SEL-BO 10% model is superior to the BO or G model when rpc for selected and non-selected SNPs is different.

the SEL-BO model is superior to the BOA and G model for estimating breeding values for purebred animals when rpc for the SNP selected to be breed-specific is different (≈20–25%) compared to rpc for the remaining SNP and when rpc for selected SNP is different (≪10–20%) compared to rpc of non-selected SNP.

the SEL-BOAs models perform similar to the BOA models and the G models, and the SEL-BOAS models are more accurate than the G models and BOA models when rpc for selected and non-selected SNPs differ from each other and from rpc estimated with the BOA model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a genomic evaluation model that is able to distinguish between selected SNP strongly associated with crossbreeding performance and the remaining SNP.
the implementation of breed-of-origin for selected SNP and the effect on the accuracy of breeding values of purebreds for crossbred performance.
a new approach for genomic evaluation of crossbred performance in a multi-breed population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BOA model is the most accurate model when the rpc for the selected SNP is larger than for the remaining SNP.
the SEL-BOAA model is not superior to the BOA and G models, however, the SEL-BOAAA model can be used when the rpc for selected and non-selected SNPs differs both (≈10 to 20%) from the G model.

the SEL-BOAs are more accurate than the BOA and the G model when (1) the rpc for the selected SNP differs strongly from the rpc for the non-selected and (2) the rpc for both groups differs strongly from the G or BOAs rpc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SEL-BOAA models are useful when rpc differs between selected and non-selected markers.
a SEL-BOA approach is useful for a crossbreeding system when the rpc differs between selected and non-selected markers and between the selected and non selected markers and the rpc differs from 1.0.
the SEL-BOAs are a promising alternative for genomic evaluation for crossbred populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SEL-BOAA model can be a good alternative to the BOA or G model when the rpc is different for the selected SNP than for the non- selected SNP and when the difference between the rpc of the selected and the non- selected SNPs is not too large.

the SEL-BOAA model is a promising model for the genomic evaluation of crossbred animals, however, it is only useful for SNP that explain a substantial proportion of the total crossbreed genetic variance.
the SEL-BOa model is a promising alternative to the BOA models when rpc is different between the selected and nonselected SNP.
